quickSummary: Glycolysis (EMP pathway) is the universal, cytosolic, oxygen-independent 10-step breakdown of 1 glucose into 2 pyruvate molecules. The Preparatory Phase (Steps 1–5) consumes 2 ATP to cleave glucose into 2 triose phosphates (GAP and DHAP), with Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1) catalyzing the key committed step. The Pay-off Phase (Steps 6–10) generates 4 ATP via substrate-level phosphorylation (PGK and Pyruvate Kinase) and 2 NADH + 2 H⁺ (GAPDH). Net yield per glucose = 2 Pyruvate + 2 ATP + 2 NADH.

summaryBox.takeaway: Glycolysis operates strictly in the cytosol. Consumes 2 ATP in the Preparatory Phase; Generates 4 ATP (Substrate-Level) + 2 NADH in the Pay-Off Phase. Net: 2 ATP + 2 NADH + 2 Pyruvate.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Glycolysis (discovered by Embden, Meyerhof, and Parnas — EMP Pathway) is the universal, oxygen-independent, 10-step enzymatic breakdown of one molecule of 6-carbon glucose into two molecules of 3-carbon Pyruvic Acid (Pyruvate) in the cytosol.

- **Universal Ancestral Pathway**: Present in all living organisms (aerobes and anaerobes alike).
- **Dual Energetic Phases**:
  1. **Preparatory Phase (Energy Investment, Steps 1–5)**: Glucose is phosphorylated twice and cleaved into two triose phosphates (Glyceraldehyde-3-Phosphate and Dihydroxyacetone Phosphate), consuming $2\text{ ATP}$.
  2. **Pay-off Phase (Energy Generation, Steps 6–10)**: Both triose phosphates are oxidized and dephosphorylated, generating $4\text{ ATP}$ and $2\text{ NADH} + 2\text{ H}^+$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.1 Glycolysis 10-Step Enzymatic Flow
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.1 Glycolysis 10-Step Enzymatic Flow
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
GLYCOLYSIS 10-STEP CASCADE
                        
   Glucose (6C) ──[1. Hexokinase + ATP]──► Glucose-6-P ──[2. Phosphohexose Isomerase]──► Fructose-6-P
                                                                                         │
   Fructose-1,6-BP ◄──[3. PFK-1 + ATP (RATE-LIMITING)]───────────────────────────────────┘
          │
  [4. Aldolase]
          │
   GAP (3C) ◄──[5. Triose Phosphate Isomerase]──► DHAP (3C)
      │ (2 Molecules of GAP enter Pay-off Phase)
      ▼
   [6. GAPDH + 2 NAD⁺ + 2 P_i] ──► 2 x 1,3-Bisphosphoglycerate + **2 NADH + 2 H⁺**
      │
   [7. Phosphoglycerate Kinase + 2 ADP] ──► 2 x 3-Phosphoglycerate + **2 ATP (SUBSTRATE-LEVEL)**
      │
   [8. Phosphoglycerate Mutase] ──► 2 x 2-Phosphoglycerate
      │
   [9. Enolase - H₂O] ──► 2 x Phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP)
      │
   [10. Pyruvate Kinase + 2 ADP] ──► 2 x Pyruvate (3C) + **2 ATP (SUBSTRATE-LEVEL)**
conceptBreakdown.content:
The 10 steps of the EMP pathway operate sequentially in the cytoplasm:

- **Step 1 (Hexokinase)**: Traps glucose inside the cell by phosphorylating it to G-6-P, utilizing $1\text{ ATP}$ and $\text{Mg}^{2+}$.
- **Step 3 (PFK-1)**: The primary committed, irreversible rate-limiting step of glycolysis, allosterically activated by AMP/ADP and inhibited by ATP and citrate.
- **Step 6 (GAPDH)**: The only oxidation step in glycolysis; GAP is oxidized while inorganic phosphate ($\text{P}_i$) is incorporated, reducing $\text{NAD}^+$ to $\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+$.
- **Steps 7 & 10 (Substrate-Level Phosphorylation)**: Phosphoglycerate Kinase and Pyruvate Kinase directly transfer high-energy phosphate groups to ADP, generating $2\text{ ATP}$ each (total $4\text{ ATP}$ gross).
- **Step 9 (Enolase)**: Dehydrates 2-PGA into PEP; specifically inhibited by Fluoride ions ($\text{F}^-$) via $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ chelation.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.2 Detailed 10-Step Glycolytic Reaction Matrix
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 Detailed 10-Step Glycolytic Reaction Matrix
conceptBreakdown.content:
### Detailed 10-Step Glycolytic Reaction Matrix

| Step | Reaction Name | Substrate $\rightarrow$ Product | Enzyme | Energy Yield / Consumption |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | Phosphorylation I | Glucose $\rightarrow$ Glucose-6-Phosphate (G-6-P) | **Hexokinase** ($\text{Mg}^{2+}$ dependent) | **Consumes $1\text{ ATP}$** |
| **2** | Isomerization | G-6-P $\rightarrow$ Fructose-6-Phosphate (F-6-P) | Phosphohexose Isomerase | None |
| **3** | Phosphorylation II | F-6-P $\rightarrow$ Fructose-1,6-Bisphosphate | **Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1)** | **Consumes $1\text{ ATP}$** *(Commitment Step)* |
| **4** | Cleavage | F-1,6-BP $\rightarrow$ GAP + DHAP | **Aldolase** | None |
| **5** | Isomerization | DHAP $\rightleftharpoons$ Glyceraldehyde-3-Phosphate (GAP) | Triose Phosphate Isomerase | None |
| **6** | Oxidation & Phosphorylation | $2\text{ GAP} + 2\text{ P}_i \rightarrow 2\text{ (1,3-BPG)}$ | **GAPDH** | **Generates $2\text{ NADH} + 2\text{ H}^+$** |
| **7** | Substrate-Level Phosphorylation I | $2\text{ (1,3-BPG)} + 2\text{ ADP} \rightarrow 2\text{ (3-PGA)}$ | **Phosphoglycerate Kinase** | **Generates $2\text{ ATP}$** |
| **8** | Shift | $2\text{ (3-PGA)} \rightarrow 2\text{ (2-PGA)}$ | Phosphoglycerate Mutase | None |
| **9** | Dehydration | $2\text{ (2-PGA)} \rightarrow 2\text{ PEP} + 2\text{ H}_2\text{O}$ | **Enolase** ($\text{Mg}^{2+}$ / Fluoride inhibited) | Releases $2\text{ H}_2\text{O}$ |
| **10** | Substrate-Level Phosphorylation II | $2\text{ PEP} + 2\text{ ADP} \rightarrow 2\text{ Pyruvate}$ | **Pyruvate Kinase** ($\text{K}^+/\text{Mg}^{2+}$) | **Generates $2\text{ ATP}$** |

$$\mathbf{\text{Net EMP Equation: Glucose} + 2\text{ NAD}^+ + 2\text{ ADP} + 2\text{ P}_i \longrightarrow 2\text{ Pyruvate} + 2\text{ NADH} + 2\text{ H}^+ + 2\text{ ATP}}$$
